trickyParts: BUILD_CACHE (type=gha,scope=envoy-${{ matrix.arch }}) is declared once in the docker job's env; cache-to is format('{0},mode=min', env.BUILD_CACHE) only on refs/heads/main.

mode=min keeps no records for intermediate stages: the Go and web stages hit only when none of their inputs changed, otherwise they rerun from their first step; the full no-cache leg is still 4.2-6.9 min.
The digest artifacts keep the repository's default retention, so a re-run of image_index or one leg still finds both digests.
deviations: Temporary commit d2605357 let the branch write its own Actions-cache scope; 99da66ef reverts it (the workflow is identical to 98a88768). The hit was measured by re-running single jobs of run 40521465193 at d2605357 right after the write, because the repository's Actions cache (12.06 GB, over the 10 GB limit) evicted the branch's entries before the final-head run 40546893651 started, which therefore measured a miss.

The round-1 GHCR tags buildcache-amd64 (version 1452720428) and buildcache-arm64 (version 1452457314) stay: nothing reads them now, and the implement App gets 403 on deleting package versions; reported to the architect.
openQuestions: A2 (7-day main median of the slower docker leg < 8 min) is proven in the production check; branch numbers: hit 2.00, miss 4.3-6.9.
discoveredComplexity: The repository's Actions cache is over its 10 GB limit (12.06 GB on 2026-10-28, oldest entry under 18 h old), so even main's envoy-<arch> entries may be evicted between runs until the pull-request cache writes stop (INFRA-520).
